Consonant list only (unsourced beyond Ethnologue); nothing on stress; no Namonuito-specific references.

sources.citation: Odango, Emerson L. 2015. Affeu fangani 'join together': a morphophonemic analysis of possessive suffix paradigms... Pakin Lukunosh Mortlockese. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.note: Mentions Nómwonweité (Namonuito) only as a place name; nothing on its phonology.

sources.citation: Ellis, S. James. 2012. Saipan Carolinian, one Chuukic language blended from many. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (hdl:10125/100894).
sources.note: Silent on Namonuito stress. States prosody of the Carolinian/Chuukic languages 'ha[s] not been researched enough to be included' (p.[129], fn.78) and that Namonuito 'is still waiting to be adequately documented' (ch.3, near Table 3-27). Reproduces Quackenbush's (1968:59) consonant-correspondence table incl. Namonuito (col. 12).

sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick H. & Jeffrey C. Marck. 1991. Carolinian-English Dictionary. PALI Language Texts: Micronesia. Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press (hdl:10125/62861).
sources.note: Introduction (p.xv) notes Tanapag-dialect speakers descend from Namonuito migrants; no statement on word stress anywhere in the front matter (only hits for 'accent' are dictionary glosses).

sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick H. 1983. The internal and external relationships of the Trukic languages of Micronesia. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii. (open scan on MPG PuRe, hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-7182-4)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: No synchronic stress statement for Namonuito (Namonuito data taken from Quackenbush 1968; Jackson's own sample excludes Pullap, Namonuito, Murilo). Only a historical claim, p.223: 'It is almost certain that Trukic had a pattern of alternating stress, beginning with the penultimate mora and assigning stress to every second mora to the left of that one' (used to explain *au reflexes).

sources.citation: Elbert, Samuel H. 1974. Puluwat Grammar. Pacific Linguistics B-29. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Single mention of the 'Namonuito dialect' (demonstratives preceding nouns); nothing on Namonuito stress.

sources.citation: Sohn, Ho-min & Byron W. Bender. 1973. A Ulithian Grammar. Pacific Linguistics C-27.
sources.note: Cites Quackenbush 1968 for Trukic vowel correspondences only; nothing on Namonuito.
